review: The base model with 8GB RAM struggles with many chrome tabs and Lightroom. Upgrades are very expensive.
Speakers are surprisingly full for such a thin machine. Webcam is clear on video calls.
Only two USB-C ports, so I'm living the dongle life again.
Super light and thin, easily the best laptop for travelling.
Battery life is unreal, I go two full days of college without charging.
Keyboard is comfortable and the trackpad is the best I've used on any laptop.
The display is sharp and colour accurate, but it's only 60Hz which feels dated at this price.
Completely silent since there's no fan, and it never gets uncomfortably hot on my lap.
MagSafe charging is so convenient, and the charger is tiny.
Wakes instantly, apps open fast, and the battery barely moves while browsing.
Driving two external monitors with the lid closed works well for my desk setup.
Performance drops during long video exports because there's no fan to cool it.
Great value when it's on sale, but the storage and memory upgrade prices are ridiculous.
Lovely laptop but the price in India is steep for the base configuration.
The notch in the screen bothered me at first but I stopped noticing it after a week.
Build quality is excellent, the aluminium body feels premium and solid.
Gaming options on macOS are very limited, most of my steam library doesn't run.
Perfect for coding and writing. Just wish it had an HDMI port.
